subject: Hybrid onramp: OEM shipment windows + cloud backstop coordination
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tony Guerrero <tony.guerrero@acmecloud.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 10:06:00 -0700
Subject: Hybrid onramp: OEM shipment windows + cloud backstop coordination

Tony / Acme ops team —

Quick context: DEAL-3921 has a Q4 product onramp target that depends on a mix of OEM-delivered blades (preferred for cost and long-term ops) and a short-term cloud backstop to hit committed capacity. We need to lock in two things this week: 1) firm ship-week ranges from OEM by tranche (how many racks, which GPU SKU per tranche, and customs/ETD assumptions), and 2) a cloud backstop offer we can include in the mutual action plan (pricing & guaranteed availability for the ramp weeks).

Attached is our provisional provisioning matrix (draft_provisioning_matrix.xlsx) showing the proposed split: 60% OEM, 40% cloud for the first 8 weeks of onramp. Key asks from Acme:
- Can you confirm a realistic ship-week range per tranche for H100 80GB / A100 80GB blades? We need earliest and latest ETA windows, and any hold-up risks (slot booking, customs, factory shifts).
- Provide a quote that separates FOB (factory) vs delivered-to-DC pricing, and identify any optional expedited lanes and their cost deltas.
- For the cloud backstop: please include a short draft (terms + price per reserved vGPU-hour, preemption policy) we can present to the customer. We need to know whether cloud capacity is modeled as firm reserved or soft backfill.

Internal note: Karthik, Ben — please review the sizing assumptions column in the spreadsheet and flag any immediate issues. Vanessa, can you coordinate procurement language if we need a partial prepay to secure OEM slot?

I’m proposing a short sync Friday (30 minutes) to reconcile timelines and finalize the MAP for the customer.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft_provisioning_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Tony Guerrero <tony.guerrero@acmecloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+procurement@acmecloud.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid onramp: OEM shipment windows + cloud backstop coordination

Laura —

Thanks for the clear ask. We pulled the latest from our logistics and sourcing teams and attached the preliminary OEM quote (Acme_OEM_Quote_0428.pdf). High level:
- Current lead time for H100 80GB blades is 11–15 weeks from Purchase Order (PO) receipt, A100 80GB is 9–12 weeks. These include our standard manufacturing buffer but exclude customs delays.
- We can split the delivery into two tranches (early partial release + bulk) but early-release inventory will incur a 6% premium; expedited manufacturing lanes are available at an incremental cost (~12–18% depending on quantity).
- Customs windows for shipments to West Coast DCs historically add 3–10 business days; we can provide an ETA corridor per DC once we have the final ship port.

Cloud backstop: we can offer a reserved pool with the following options (drafted in the attached doc):
- Firm reserved vGPU pool: 24/7 dedicated tenancy, 99.5% availability, quoted at $X per vGPU-hour with a minimum 3-month commitment.
- Soft backfill: on-demand capacity with priority access and a 48-hour rollback clause; lower cost but no strict SLA.

We're open to a mixed approach — reserve enough cloud to cover the first 4 weeks while OEM fills up the remainder. Note: to lock the OEM tranche windows we will need a PO with partial deposit or an agreed reservation fee to hold factory slots.

I’ll join Friday’s sync. Attaching: Acme_OEM_Quote_0428.pdf and proposed_cloud_backstop_terms.docx.

Best,
Tony Guerrero
Strategic Accounts — AcmeCloud
tony.guerrero@acmecloud.com | +1 206-555-0147

Attachments: Acme_OEM_Quote_0428.pdf (PDF stub), proposed_cloud_backstop_terms.docx (docx stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid onramp: OEM shipment windows + cloud backstop coordination

Laura / team —

Quick technical and ops read on Tony’s numbers: they map to what we’ve seen across other deals but we should tighten SKU mix and tranche sizing before we commit deposits. Specifics:
- SKU choice: If the workload tolerates a 6–8% perf delta we can prioritize A100 80GB for the first tranche (faster availability), and schedule H100 for the bulk. That reduces the earliest ETA by ~2–4 weeks and keeps costs lower.
- Quantities we asked for in the spreadsheet assume 24 racks (576 GPUs) total for initial onramp. Proposed split: 10 racks (A100) in tranche 1, 14 racks (H100) tranche 2. Please confirm if the customer can accept mixed SKU now vs a homogeneous fleet.
- Cloud backstop sizing: recommend reserving 40% of peak vGPU-hours for weeks 1–4, then step down to 15–20% weeks 5–8. That maps to Tony’s 3-month reserved pricing for a short-term commitment.

Action items for procurement/legal/finance:
- Vanessa: can procurement prepare a reservation fee term sheet (amount & refundable terms)? Estimate: 10% slot-hold fee on tranche 1 value.
- Ben: start finance run-rate to model capex vs near-term OPEX delta for the mixed approach — I’ll paste the adjusted quantities into the spreadsheet and label as SIZING_V2.

If we want OEM to commit to specific ship-week corridors we should be ready to put a PO with the tranche and pay the slot-hold fee within 5 business days. Otherwise we risk slipping to the next manufacturing window.

Karthik
Director, Capacity Strategy — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tony Guerrero <tony.guerrero@acmecloud.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid onramp: OEM shipment windows + cloud backstop coordination

Team / Tony —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the detail. Summary and agreed next steps (actionable items for the MAP):

1) SKU/tranche decision (owner: Karthik) — Karthik to confirm by EOD Tuesday whether customer accepts mixed SKUs (A100 first tranche / H100 bulk). If yes, Karthik will upload SIZING_V2 to HubSpot and confirm final rack counts.

2) Reservation fee and PO timing (owner: Vanessa) — Vanessa to draft reservation fee term sheet (10% tranche-1 hold fee, refundable less reasonable restocking costs) and an expedited PO template for legal review. Target: finalize fee term sheet Wednesday COB.

3) Cloud backstop (owner: Tony / Acme) — Tony to deliver a final quoted line-item for a 4-week reserved pool (hourly rate + SLA) and a short addendum we can attach to our MAP. Target: revised doc by Wednesday.

4) Finance modeling (owner: Ben) — Ben to produce a brief capex vs opex comparison (including expedited premium scenarios) for the Friday exec sync.

5) Sync cadence — 30-minute alignment Friday 09:00 PT (internal + Tony). Please flag any schedule conflicts now.

I’ve attached an updated MAP (MAP-Q4_onramp_v2.pdf) with the timeline placeholders and tasks. Once we have Tony’s final backstop terms and Vanessa’s reservation language we can circulate a single MAP to the customer and request PO authorization.

Thanks everyone — let’s keep the windows tight on these deliverables.

Laura
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
